Report on Illegal Functioning of Japanese Military Gendarme in the International Settlement. -------------------------------------------------- At 3.25p.m. 8-1-39, a telephone message was received from the Dollar Hotel, No. 69 Yu Ya Ching Road reporting a number of plain clothes Japanese searching Room No. 405 with the apparent intention of making an arrest. The undersigned and C.D.S. 192 attended and found 2 Japanese plain clothes men inside Room 405 and 2 in the corridor nearby. When asked for an explanation they made no reply and indicated that they neither spoke English or Chinese. A Japanese interpreter was then summoned from Central Station and in the interval of waiting the various Chinese employees of the hotel who were concerned in this case were interviewed. Wong Ah Ching (王亞卿), Steward, Loh Yuen Loong (陸元龍), Floor inspector. Soo Kyung Yue (蘇金友), teaboy for Room 405. all having seen the original occupant of Room 405 were of the opinion that he was a Cantonese or Fokienese although he signed the hotel register as being a native of Shanghai. The above 3 Chinese have submitted statements which are attached hereto and are self explanatory.

At about 4.30 p.m. J.P.C. 220 Mawatari arrived from Central Station and the 4 Japanese were asked to explain their business.

They identified themselves as members of the Japanese Military Gendarme and stated they wanted to see a friend in Room 405.

In view of the statement of the Hotel employees this statement did not seem feasible so the four men were asked to attend Chengtu Road Station and make a proper report and obtain assistance if they wished to function in the Settlement.

The 4 men did not wish to attend Chengtu Road Station but after some considerable argument were persuaded to do so, one of the men however disappeared down the back stairs and could not be located.

C.D.S. 192 was posted inside the room to keep observation. | |

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The three Japanese who came to the station with the undersigned and two others who visited room 405 a few minutes later and who were brought in by J.D.S. 250 and J.D.S. 289 were questioned by J.D.S. Yoshinaga and identified themselves as follows:-

(1) Warrant Officer Hideo Kubota (久保田英男)
(2) Sergeant Major Takeo Yamatsu (山津武夫)
(3) Corporal Jinpei Tamura (田村金平)
(4) Corporal Toshiro Yokoyama (横畑利郎)
(5) Mr. Ishitatsu Ozawa (小津牛郎)

The 1st to 4th listed are members of the North Szechuen Road Branch office of the Japanese Army Gendarme and the 5th listed is a civilian assistant.

The men were then asked their reason for being in the Dollar Hotel and Warrant-officer Hideo Kubota, who acted as spokesman for the party, replied that they were in the hotel to protect a Japanese subject who was of unsound mind and in possession of a great deal of money.

At this stage the D.I.O. "A" who had previously been informed arrived and conducted enquiries, the following being ascertained:-

The above 5 plain clothes men had been despatched to the Dollar Hotel to effect the arrest of a Japanese subject named Tsutomu Makino, a Japanese army employee who had absconded with 8,500 yen.

随署人一同来到捕房的三名日本人，以及几分钟后访问405号房间并由日本侦探警员（J.D.S.）250号和289号带回来的另外两人，接受了日本侦探警员（J.D.S.）吉永（Yoshinaga，音译）的讯问，并表明身份如下：-

(1) 准尉 久保田英男 (Hideo Kubota)
(2) 曹长 山津武夫 (Takeo Yamatsu)
(3) 伍长 田村金平 (Jinpei Tamura)
(4) 伍长 横畑利郎 (Toshiro Yokoyama)
(5) 小津牛郎 (Ishitatsu Ozawa) 先生

名单中第1至第4人为大日本帝国陆军宪兵队北四川路分遣队成员，第5人为平民助手。

随后询问他们出现在达华饭店的原因，作为该团体发言人的准尉久保田英男回答说，他们在饭店是为了保护一名精神失常且持有大量钱财的日本臣民。

此时，此前已获通知的“A”分区督察主任（D.I.O. "A"）抵达并展开调查，查明情况如下：-

上述5名便衣男子被派往达华饭店，旨在逮捕一名名为牧野勉（Tsutomu Makino，音译）的日本臣民，此人为日军雇员，携款8,500日元潜逃。

CRIME REGISTER No:— ____________________ Division. ____________________ Police Station. .................................................... 19 Diary Number:— 1/4 Nature of Offence: ____________________ | Time at which investigation begun and concluded each day | RECORD OF INVESTIGATION. | Places visited in course of investigation each day | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | | Sgt. Major Takeo Nametsu stated they were not concerned about the recovery of the money but merely wished to protect Mr. Makino who being a mental case might be robbed or otherwise cheated out of the money.

The D.D.C. informed the 5 men that if they wished to make an arrest in the Settlement they must have proper assistance from Headquarters.

It was finally agreed that the Japanese should not return to the Dollar Hotel without assistance but that a S.M.P. detective should be posted in Room 405 and, should the wanted man or any of his associates (Japanese named Takaha and Kido), return, the Japanese Gendarme would be informed immediately.

At 7 p.m. Major Merritt A. Edson and Major J.S. Monohan of the U.S. Marine Corps (who had previously been informed by order of D.D.C. "A"), attended the station and requested particulars. The facts of the case were explained to the 2 officers and they stated that they were only interested in whether or not the Japanese Military Police were carrying arms in the American Sector.

The 5 Japanese voluntarily took off their coats in the presence of the above U.S.M.C. officers who stated they were satisfied that no arms were being carried. | |

副总监（D.D.C.）告知这5人，若希望在租界内实施逮捕，必须获得总办事处的适当协助。

最终达成协议，日本人不得在无协助的情况下返回达华饭店，但应派遣一名工部局警务处（S.M.P.）侦探驻守405号房间，一旦通缉犯或其任何同伙（名为高桥 Takaha 和木户 Kido 的日本人）返回，将立即通知日本宪兵队。

晚上7点，美国海军陆战队（U.S. Marine Corps）的梅里特·A·埃德森（Merritt A. Edson）少校和 J.S. 莫诺汉（J.S. Monohan）少校（此前已按“A”分区副总监命令通知）来到捕房并要求了解详情。向这两名军官解释了案件事实，他们表示只关心日本宪兵是否在美国防区内携带武器。

在上述美国海军陆战队军官面前，5名日本人自愿脱下外套，军官们表示满意，确认未携带武器。 | |

FORM 40
G. 20M 1 38

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Loh Yuen Loong.
native of Shanghai taken by me J.D.S. 192
translated
at Jin. Rd. Stn. on the 8-1-39 and interpreted by Clerk Tan.

Loh Yuen Loong, 28, Shanghai, single.
I am an Inspector employed at and residin' on the Dollar
Hotel, No. 69 Yu Ya Ching Road.
At 3.45 p.m. on the 8-1-39, while I was in the hall down-
stairs, I observed 5 persons resembling Japanese come in and go
up in the lift. (I knew they were Japanese by the fact that
one of them wore muzzle). I followed them up and saw them enter
Room No. 407. I also went in and observed the 5 intruders
search everything in the room which indicated their intention
to arrest some person. I questioned them as to where they came
from and one of them replied me that "They were Japanese Mili-
tary Police. Confidential! Confidential!"
Fearing that some incident might happen, I rushed to the
accountant's office from where I telephoned to the Chengtu Road
Station.
Later, detectives from the above station attended and
brought the 5 intruders to the station.
The above is my true statement.

Signed.

警方调查报告。

以下为陆元龙的陈述。
上海籍，由我，日本侦探警员（J.D.S.）192号，
翻译
于1939年1月8日在静安寺路捕房录取，由谭职员口译。

陆元龙，28岁，上海人，未婚。
我是受雇于虞洽卿路69号达华饭店的巡视员，并居住于此。
1939年1月8日下午3:45，当我在楼下大厅时，我观察到5名貌似日本人的人进来并乘电梯上楼。（我知道他们是日本人，因为其中一人戴着口罩。）我跟随他们上楼，看见他们进入407号房间。我也进去观察，看到这5名闯入者搜查房间内的所有物品，这表明他们意图逮捕某人。我质问他们来自何处，其中一人回答我说：“我们是日本宪兵。机密！机密！”
担心可能发生事端，我冲到会计室，从那里打电话给成都路捕房。
随后，上述捕房的侦探赶到，并将5名闯入者带到捕房。
以上是我的真实陈述。

签名。

FORM 40

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Wong An Ching.
native of Ningpo taken by me J.D.S. 192
translated
at Che. Rd. Stn. on the 8-1-39 and interpreted by Clerk Tan.

Wong An Ching, 46, Ningpo, married, residing No. 35 Van
Yih Li Myburgh Road.
I am a steward employed by the Dollar Hotel, located at
69 Yu Ya Ching Road.
At 12 noon on the 7-1-39, while I was in the Reception
Room, a stranger who may be described as follows:-
"Long thin face, dark complexion, long parted hair,
wearing black woollen foreign dress, black woollen overcoat,
and black spectacles, has short mustache."
approached me enquiring about any vacant room in Shanghai
dialect. Answering him in the affirmative, I guided the stranger
to Room No. 405 on the 4th floor which he, after a glance, booked.
He asked me how much he needed to pay first and I told him to
pay $6.00 which he did. I then instructed Teaboy No. 409 named
Joo Kyung Yue to bring the customer the Hotel Register to fill
in and upon this being brought to the customer, the latter wrote
his surname "Zeu" on it.
However, above the character "Zeu", I witnessed the
customer write his name "Wong Tsung Fi, 48, Shanghai, Merchant,"
Having completed my duty, I returned to the Reception Room.
At about 5.30 p.m. on the 8-1-39 I made a statement at the
Chengtu Road Police Station giving the whole facts as above
mentioned.
The above is my true statement.

Signed & cross-marked.

以下为王亚卿的陈述。
宁波籍，由我，日本侦探警员（J.D.S.）192号，
翻译
于1939年1月8日在成都路捕房录取，由谭职员口译。

王亚卿，46岁，宁波人，已婚，居住于迈尔西爱路（Myburgh Road）范义里35号。
我是受雇于虞洽卿路69号达华饭店的服务员。
1939年1月7日中午12点，当我在接待室时，一名陌生人，其特征描述如下：-
“长瘦脸，肤色黝黑，长发中分，身穿黑色羊毛西装，黑色羊毛大衣，戴黑框眼镜，留短胡须。”
用上海话向我询问是否有空房。我给予肯定答复后，引导该陌生人到四楼405号房间，他看了一眼后便预订了。
他问我需要先付多少钱，我告诉他付6美元，他照办了。随后我指示409号茶房朱金友（Joo Kyung Yue，音译，注：前文为苏金友 Soo Kyung Yue）拿饭店登记簿给客人填写，当登记簿递给客人后，后者在上面写下了姓氏“Zeu”。
然而，在“Zeu”字上方，我目睹客人写下他的名字“王宗菲（Wong Tsung Fi，音译），48岁，上海，商人”。
完成职责后，我回到接待室。
1939年1月8日下午约5:30，我在成都路捕房作了陈述，详述了上述事实。
以上是我的真实陈述。

签名并画押。

FORM 40
G. 308 I 38

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Soo Kyung Yue
native of Ningpo taken by me J.T.S. 19E
translated
at Ch. Rd. Stn. on the 8-1-39 and interpreted by Clerk Tan.

Soo Kyung Yue, 31, Ningpo, married, residing in an up-stairs room of the Johnson Hire Car Service, Peking Road.

At 11.10 p.m. on the 7-1-39, Steward Jong Ah Ching instructed me to bring the Hotel Register to a customer to fill and when I got the Hotel Register, I went to Room No. 405 in which I saw a customer who may be described as follows:-
"Long face, dark complexion, wearing black woollen foreign dress and black woollen overcoat."

The customer accordingly wrote his name "Zeu" on it. I then got the tea ready and delivered it to the above numbered room. Having done this, I returned the Hotel Register to the Account office. I did not enter the room afterwards and, if anybody has visited the room I do not know.

At 6 p.m. same date, I went off duty.

At 9 a.m. on the 8-1-39, I came on duty and at about 10a.m. a teeboy No. 407 informed me that the customer in Room No. 405 had ordered 3 refreshments but I did not go to the room.

At 11a.m. I received a telephone message from the Account Office to the effect that the car hired by the customer in Room No. 405 has arrived. I went to the room and informed the customer who booked the room yesterday and he said he knew it. I then went to Room 424 to work. I did not see when the customer left his room.

At 3.45 p.m. on the 8-1-39 I saw that there were Japanese subjects in the hotel besides Foreign and Chinese Detectives.

At 5.30 p.m. same date, I attended the Chengtu Road Police Station, where I made this statement.

The above is true
Signed.

表格 40
G. 308 I 38

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为本人 J.T.S.（19E巡捕）于1939年1月8日在成都路捕房，由谭姓书记员翻译所记录的宁波籍人士 Soo Kyung Yue 的供词。

Soo Kyung Yue，31岁，宁波人，已婚，居住在北京路 Johnson 出租汽车服务行楼上的房间。

1939年1月7日晚上11点10分，服务员 Jong Ah Ching 指示我将旅馆登记簿带给一位顾客填写。当我拿到旅馆登记簿后，我前往405号房间，在那里我看到一位顾客，其外貌特征如下：
“长脸，肤色黝黑，身穿黑色毛料西装和黑色毛料大衣。”

该顾客随即在登记簿上写下名字“Zeu”。随后我备好茶水并送至上述房间。做完这些后，我将旅馆登记簿交回会计室。此后我没有再进入该房间，如果有人去过该房间，我也不知情。

同日晚上6点，我下班。

1939年1月8日上午9点，我上班。大约上午10点，407号茶房告诉我，405号房间的顾客点了三份茶点，但我没有去该房间。

上午11点，我接到会计室的电话通知，称405号房间顾客预订的汽车已到达。我前往该房间通知昨天预订房间的顾客，他说他知道了。随后我去424号房间工作。我没有看到该顾客离开房间的时间。

1939年1月8日下午3点45分，我看到酒店里除了外籍和华人侦探外，还有日本籍人士。

同日下午5点30分，我前往成都路捕房，在此作了上述陈述。

以上属实
签名。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT

HEADQUARTERS CRIME BRANCH

G. I. MISCELLANEOUS FILE
No. 6139

Date January 9, 39.
19

Subject ASSISTANCE RENDERED TO THE JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
D. I. REGISTRY
No: S. B. D. __________
Date __________

Made by & Forwarded by.

Sir,

At about 9:45 p.m. January 8th. 1939, J.D.C.
Yamahara of the S/M.C. Staff informed the undersigned that
Sgt. Tamura of the Japanese Gendarmerie had requested assistance
to arrest two Japanese subjects, who were wanted for "mis-
appropriation."

The necessary assistance was rendered by the
undersigned, and with the cooperation of two Chinese detectives
attached to Route Station, visited Room No.308, the Great
Eastern" Hotel, Nanking Road, where one, named J. KIDO (Japanese)
aged 38 years, was taken into custody.

On being questioned, this man stated that his
accomplice, another Japanese subject, named T. H. KINO, was then
residing in Room No.405, the "Dollar" Hotel, 69 Yu Ya Ching Rd.

With the assistance of D.I. Hill, this
address was visited, but it was found that the wanted man had
already left. According to D.I. Hill, this address had already
been visited by the Gendarmerie that afternoon.

From further information given by the arrested
man, House No.12, Lane 125, Park Road, was visited, but the
wanted man was not located. In this case, Sinza Station was
informed, and F.S. Wittinsky attended with a Chinese detective.

In view of the fact that the arrested man,
J. KIDO is a Japanese subject, he was handed over direct to the
authorities concerned.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

D. C. (Special Branch). D. I.

（左侧手写批注：1407 9/1）

G. I. 杂项档案

捕房，___
日期 1939年1月9日。
19

事由：协助日本宪兵队。

上海公共租界工部局警务处
侦探情报处登记室
编号：S. B. D. ___
日期 ___

制作及呈报人。

先生，

1939年1月8日晚约9点45分，工部局职员 Yamahara 先生告知本人，日本宪兵队的 Tamura 警士请求协助逮捕两名因“挪用公款”而被通缉的日本籍人士。

本人提供了必要的协助，并在两名隶属于路线捕房的华探的配合下，前往南京路“大东方”酒店（Great Eastern Hotel）308号房间，将一名名为 J. KIDO（日本人），38岁的男子拘捕。

经讯问，该男子供述其同伙，另一名名为 T. H. KINO 的日本籍人士，当时居住在虞洽卿路69号“美元”酒店（Dollar Hotel）405号房间。

在侦探情报处 Hill 先生的协助下，我们走访了该地址，但发现被通缉者已经离开。据 Hill 先生称，宪兵队当天下午已经走访过该地址。

根据被捕男子提供的进一步线索，我们走访了派克路125弄12号，但未找到被通缉者。在此情况下，我们通知了新闸捕房，F.S. Wittinsky 与一名华探一同前往处理。

鉴于被捕者 J. KIDO 为日本籍人士，他被直接移交给有关当局。

此致，
敬礼，

D. C. （特务科）。侦探情报处。

（左侧手写批注：1407 9/1）
（底部手写签名及日期：S / 9/1 ... C / 10 ...）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

Date Feb. 13, 1939.
Subject. ARREST OF NATIVES IN CONNECTION WITH JAPANESE
C. I. D. III.
Made by // __________ Forwarded by J. D. S. I. UMEMOTO.

In reference to the letter from the Liangyin
Fellow Countrymen's Association regarding the de-
tention of : -

WANG CHUNG YI (王种英) (alias WANG CHIEN).
TS'AO YU CH'I (曹耀奎) and his wife
TS'AO P'AN SHIH (曹潘氏)

who were arrested on Jan. 4, 1939, as also were
six others at various addresses in the Settlement —

CH'EN O SHIH (陈顾氏)
LIU TZU MING (刘子明)
HU YUNG AN (胡永安) (died in custody on 30.1.39)
TSAO SHIH CHUNG (左士中)
HU YU I (胡玉義)
YÜ HUA CH'ANG (華常)

— no evidence of complicity in Anti-Japanese activities
has been produced against them by the Japanese Gen-
darmerie, nor have the latter, since Jan. 4, made
any direct requests to C.I. for the arrested persons
to be handed over.

J.D.S.I. Umemoto has again visited the Japanese
Military Police H.Qrs. at Bridge House regarding
the disposal of these people and their attitude
is that if the Police want to release them they
may do so, but if the latter will agree they would
like them to be handed over for enquiry. However,
the Military do not insist that this should be done.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）
（批：Penny/2）
（批：S/ [签名]）

关于两广同乡会来信提及拘留以下人员一事：-

WANG CHUNG YI (王种英)（别名 WANG CHIEN）。
TS'AO YU CH'I (曹耀奎) 及其妻子
TS'AO P'AN SHIH (曹潘氏)

他们于1939年1月4日被捕，同时在租界内不同地址被捕的还有另外六人——

CH'EN O SHIH (陈顾氏)
LIU TZU MING (刘子明)
HU YUNG AN (胡永安)（于1939年1月30日在羁押期间死亡）
TSAO SHIH CHUNG (左士中)
HU YU I (胡玉義)
YÜ HUA CH'ANG (華常)

— 日本宪兵队未能提供他们参与反日活动的共谋证据，且自1月4日以来，后者未直接向刑事侦缉处提出移交被捕者的要求。

J.D.S.I. Umemoto 再次前往百老汇大厦的日本军警总部，就处置这些人一事进行交涉，他们的态度是，如果警方希望释放他们，可以这样做；但如果警方同意，日方希望将他们移交以便审讯。然而，军方并不坚持必须这样做。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处）
